task.title: Bound memory cleanup analysis and report real progress
task.source: Direct user report reproduced against Harlequin on the Raspberry Pi

coreClaim: Tidy Memories still reviews every eligible memory for low-value junk, while one analysis performs at most twelve model-assisted consolidation calls and reports completed work to the user.
rootCause: Value review used the consolidation batch size and consolidation candidate generation had no per-analysis budget, so Harlequin's 94 eligible memories expanded into an upper bound of 181 sequential provider calls.

inScope: Focused scale, progress, sequential-order, and cancellation coverage
outOfScope: Memory apply, undo, or persistence behavior

claimBoundary.coreClaim: A Harlequin-scale cleanup reviews all 94 eligible memories in three value-review calls, runs at most twelve consolidation calls, remains sequential and cancellable, and reports completed groups without applying memory changes.
entrypoints: Character Memories -> Tidy memories -> Analyze memories
legacyPathsOrFormats: Exact duplicates remain detected deterministically across all eligible sources.
Cleanup proposals remain review-only until the user explicitly applies selected changes.
Analysis remains sequential and AbortSignal cancellation remains authoritative.
Existing source eligibility and similarity thresholds are unchanged.
outOfScopeClaims: This change does not make provider latency instantaneous.
This change does not apply or delete memories automatically.
This change does not guarantee every possible consolidation appears in one pass.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: A read-only cleanup preview could expand a moderate memory set into hundreds of sequential provider calls while the UI displayed only an indefinite spinner.
contractLaneGate.producer: src/engine/entities/memory-maintenance.ts candidate preparation and src/engine/generation/memory-cleanup.ts analysis loop
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: Analyze memories should finish in a bounded amount of provider work, inspect all eligible rows for junk, remain cancellable, and disclose meaningful progress.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: Value review packs up to 32 records within the existing 12000-character limit, candidate preparation returns at most 12 consolidation groups with a deferred count, and the generation loop reports initial and post-call progress.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The mode-neutral TypeScript engine owns candidate budgeting, sequential provider calls, and progress truth.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not fake timer progress, add provider concurrency, skip low-value review rows, or change storage/apply behavior.
regressionProof: The Harlequin-scale preparation test covers all 94 value-review IDs exactly once in three groups and caps consolidation at twelve groups.
The generation test proves exact progress from zero through all sequential calls.
Hook and modal tests prove visible progress and cancellation cleanup.

positiveRows.claim: Every eligible Harlequin-scale source is still reviewed for low value.
positiveRows.evidence: The 94-row regression asserts three value groups whose flattened IDs contain all 94 source IDs exactly once.

positiveRows.claim: Provider work is bounded and sequential.
positiveRows.evidence: Preparation caps consolidation groups at 12, while generation tests assert the capped request count and max one active provider call.

positiveRows.claim: The displayed counter reflects successful provider calls.
positiveRows.evidence: The engine test asserts progress 0/3, 1/3, 2/3, 3/3; hook and modal tests assert propagation and visible copy.

contradictionRows.claim: The budget must not skip junk review rows.
contradictionRows.evidence: Only consolidation candidates are deferred; value groups cover every eligible source exactly once.

contradictionRows.claim: Cancellation must not leave stale progress or show a completed preview.
contradictionRows.evidence: The hook regression cancels an in-flight analysis, asserts null progress and idle phase, then resolves the stale request without changing state.

contradictionRows.claim: Analysis must not mutate memory data.
contradictionRows.evidence: The changed engine path only returns a preview; memory apply, undo, API, and storage files are untouched.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Exact duplicate cleanup remains deterministic and does not require a consolidation model call.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Existing exact-duplicate engine tests pass unchanged.
The focused memory preparation, generation, hook, and modal suites pass all 57 tests.

untestedRows: The final Pi browser flow will be manually observable after the exact merged image is deployed; no live provider analysis is started automatically.

ownedFacts.description: The live Harlequin scope contained 94 eligible active or pinned memory rows totaling 10803 content characters.
ownedFacts.evidence: Read-only Pi inspection before the user cancelled the stalled analysis.

ownedFacts.description: The deployed implementation prepared 12 value groups and 169 consolidation groups, for an upper bound of 181 sequential provider calls.
ownedFacts.evidence: The deployed candidate preparation was run against the live Harlequin rows without applying changes.

ownedFacts.description: No cleanup apply or undo write occurred during the cancelled analysis.
ownedFacts.evidence: Pi runtime logs showed structured analysis calls and no memory apply or undo invocation.

verification.baselineEvidence: pnpm check passed with the supported DISCOVERY_CHECK_ALLOW_MISSING=1 local marker; the PR body records Feature Discoverability N/A for an existing workflow bugfix. Focused suites passed 57 tests.
negativeRowsTested: All value-review IDs appear exactly once
Consolidation groups beyond the budget are deferred
Cancelled analysis clears and ignores stale progress

notes: No user memory content is included in this ledger.
The visible counter is covered at the component boundary; post-deployment interactive browser validation remains a manual observation.
